headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API/network access plus Copilot’s repo-write capabilities create default risks of data leakage and cascading errors when paired.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while RD-Agent can browse and call APIs, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry attacker-controlled text between them. No shared clipboard/MCP is documented, and Copilot’s self-isolation reduces direct hijack risk, so this stays low.
conditions: IF RD-Agent writes prompt-like content into files that Copilot later reads, injection becomes plausible.
IF an operator manually copies RD-Agent output into Copilot chat, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Review any RD-Agent-generated text before pasting into Copilot.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated logs into prompts.
Use read-only exports for RD-Agent outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, logs, and multiple API keys. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive material can flow into Copilot’s vendor backend by default, so the pair creates a medium leakage path.
conditions: IF RD-Agent stores datasets, logs, or secrets in the same repo/workspace Copilot reads, leakage occurs.
IF Copilot is allowed to index those files, sensitive content can be transmitted to its backend.
mitigations: Separate sensitive RD-Agent artifacts from Copilot-visible folders.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace immediately.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repos only.
Rotate any API keys that were present in shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, and RD-Agent also has broad API access plus file logging. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and commits can conflict even with multiple instances supported, because neither profile shows locking or coordination across the pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, conflicting writes are possible.
IF RD-Agent writes logs while Copilot edits the same files, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Keep RD-Agent logs outside the repo.
Use manual review before git commits.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits that a human may apply, and RD-Agent is a research automation agent that can consume outputs and act via APIs. If RD-Agent treats Copilot-generated code or analysis as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or commits without verification.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests Copilot output without validation, incorrect assumptions can propagate.
IF Copilot-generated edits are committed and then used by RD-Agent, the error chain extends downstream.
mitigations: Require human verification of Copilot output before use.
Add a validation step before RD-Agent acts on generated text.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis for Copilot outputs.
Compare outputs against source data before execution.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and vendor APIs, while RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple external model APIs. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into the shared workflow, differing retention and vendor-processing terms can create a compliance mismatch; the pairwise risk is inferred from documented data classes, not a specific policy conflict.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential financial data enters the shared workflow, compliance review is required.
IF retention or deletion obligations apply to RD-Agent logs, vendor-side processing by Copilot may conflict.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot-visible context.
Use synthetic or redacted datasets in RD-Agent.
Document retention and deletion rules for shared artifacts.
Review vendor DPAs before processing sensitive data.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads by environment.
